I don't have any pictures on me as I'm at work, but I want to convert my garage into a room/ man cave.

In terms of insulation, ventilation and comfort.

What are some cheap items that would really help out? e.g Carpet? Wooden floor? New walls?

The first questions that come to my mind are:

  1. Is the garage insulated? If it is you don't need new walls,
  2. What size is it?
  3. Do you ever want to open the garage door again?

For the floor, I would do Concrete Stain. It is cheaper than both carpet and wooden floors and will allow it to stay cool

Check Here to see how to do it.

1. No, it has a back door that seals well but the actual garage door and the walls are paper thin and not insulated.
  2. It's quite large, you could probably fit three cars in there, front to back not side to side.
  3. No, I prefer to park my cark in the driveway, there's cover there anyway.

1. After we sealed our's off, we wished we had insulated and ran a duct in to the garage.
  2. Our's was only a 1 car garage so that makes a big difference.
  3. If the cover is over the front of the garage, you may get by, but if you want it done well, insulate and run a duct into it if your A/C can handle cooling and heating an additional room.

If could do mine over again,

  1. I would remove a small portion of one wall's sheetrock and find some good insulation and see how hard it will for me to insulate and re tape and float the walls
  2. I would remove the garage door opener and and track if you really think you will not need it anymore.
  3. I would remove the sheetrock on all the walls (maybe 1/4 of the room each week)
  4. I would insulate and re tape and float the existing walls. Split this up into what you can afford each week maybe do 1/4 each week
  5. I would build a frame over the garage door so you can tape and float and insulate that area too. (we used a metal frame, I wish we had used wood. )
  6. I would put a ceiling fan light combo in to make sure the air can move around ok.
  7. I would texture and paint the walls
  8. I would do the concrete stain because it is very inexpensive and will keep the floors very cool.
  9. I would consider running the duct in to the room.

In short, if I was you, I would start withe the Sheetrock, and insulation and go from there, is is cheap and will make a big difference, But remember,, I am going from my experience with a 1 car garage and I live in the deep south so heat in the room was always an issue but only after we sealed the garage door.
